name: Depth Bubble Cursor
summary: A semi-transparent sphere whose size depends only on its depth; of the objects it touches, the one closest to its centre is selected, and objects in front of it turn semi-transparent.
howItWorks: Unlike the 3D Bubble Cursor, the sphere does not shrink to fit a single object: its size changes only with depth, set with the scroll wheel, while the mouse moves it in x and y. Among the objects inside it, the one nearest to the centre is selected and highlighted. Objects in front of the cursor's depth become semi-transparent. In the study with 20 participants it was fastest in every analysis and was rated best overall, ahead of the 3D Bubble Cursor.
advantages: Fastest and best rated in the study.
Its constant size at a given depth makes it easy to keep track of.
limitations: Relies on the selected object changing colour for feedback.

relationships.note: Keeps the sphere's size tied to depth instead of fitting it to the nearest object, and picks the object closest to its centre.
Introduced and compared in the same study.
A semi-transparent volume cursor moved with a mouse.
